rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice for playfully cheeky behaviour, especially when it is endearing rather than rude.

example.english: That kid is really cheeky and always hides to scare me.
example.traditional: 個細路仔真係頑皮，成日匿埋嚇我。
example.jyutping: go3 sai3 lou6 zai2 zan1 hai6 waan4 pei4 seng4 jat6 nei1 maai4 haak3 ngo5

rows.note: Use this when the cheekiness is cocky, impertinent, or involves talking back, rather than merely playful.

example.english: You’re so cheeky—how dare you talk back to the teacher?
example.traditional: 你咁串，仲夠膽同老師頂嘴？
example.jyutping: nei5 gam3 cyun3 zung6 gau3 daam2 tung4 lou5 si1 ding2 zeoi2

rows.note: Use this for amusingly cheeky cleverness or mischievous tricks, with a lighter and more playful tone.

example.english: They were cheeky and pranked me, pretending nothing happened.
example.traditional: 佢鬼馬咁整蠱我，扮到好似冇事咁。
example.jyutping: keoi5 gwai2 maa5 gam2 zing2 gu2 ngo5 baan6 dou3 hou2 ci5 mou5 si6 gam2

rows.note: Use this only when the cheekiness is brazen or shameless, not when it is simply playful.

example.english: You’re so cheeky—you ate all my fries and still asked me for more.
example.traditional: 你真係厚面皮，食晒我啲薯條仲問我攞。
example.jyutping: nei5 zan1 hai6 hau5 min6 pei4 sik6 saai3 ngo5 di1 syu4 tiu4 zung6 man6 ngo5 lo2
